rationale: EXPORTS_JAVA2 (M14 ontology), Part 1 question 5. JLS 15.13 lets the receiver of `X::m` be ANY expression, and a real corpus writes them: measured on java-lib's 3,275 files, 15 emitted `references` endpoints were source text rather than names — a parenthesised call with its arguments (`newArrayList(v3(), v4())`), a chained call (`MultimapBuilder.linkedHashKeys().arrayListValues()`) and a STRING LITERAL (`"com.google.common."::length`, whose CONTENTS would have landed in the graph). None can join to a symbol. The contract pinned here: publish the receiver when a base name is derivable from a NAME-BEARING node, publish NOTHING when it is an expression. `ImmutableList.Builder::add` is the case that keeps the lane honest — the grammar spells a qualified receiver `field_access`, not `scoped_type_identifier`, and an over-narrow whitelist drops 68 VALID rows while looking like it removed 15 invalid ones. `this.field::hashCode` is the case that keeps it honest in the other direction: a `this` link is refused, because `this` names the enclosing instance rather than a type. Two mutants in this lane's history are pinned by these rows — a chain walk that tested `!cur` for failure rejected every chain (68 rows lost), and a text fallback inside the base-name extractor put `this.field` back.

forbidRelationships.comment: an EXPRESSION receiver has no name: `Widget.create()::hashCode` writes a call, so no receiver edge may be published
same: a chained call is not a name
a STRING LITERAL's contents are not a name; reading it here is exactly what the tree walk exists to prevent
a `this` link names the enclosing instance, not a type — refused link by link, not only when the whole name is the keyword
the METHOD side of a method reference is a `calls` target, never a `references` receiver
